verified.resolved_title: Strengthening the migrant-friendliness of Thai health services through interpretation and cultural mediation: a system analysis.
verified.note: Abstract confirms Thai MHW/MHV interpretation and cultural mediation system analysis via 50 key informants in two migrant-populated provinces. Confirms 'operational challenges in providing services included insufficient budgets for employment and training, diverse training curricula, and lack of legal provisions' -- matches claim's 'constraints in budget, training, system status' exactly.

verified.resolved_title: A Systematic Scoping Review on Migrant Health Coverage in Thailand.
verified.note: '101 articles were included in the final analysis' matches the '101 studies' claim exactly. However, the abstract states reproductive/maternal health (n=31) was the SECOND most-studied health domain, after 'health in broader terms' (n=42), not simply among 'most-studied categories' without qualification. Suggested fix: 'reproductive/maternal health among the top-studied categories (second only to general health, n=31 vs 42 studies)' rather than unqualified 'most-studied'.

verified.resolved_title: The perceptions and practices of Thai health professionals providing maternity care for migrant Burmese women: An ethnographic study.
verified.note: Ethnographic study in Ranong Province, southern Thailand; 13 healthcare professionals + 10 Burmese women, 130h observation. Theme 'The system is in control' with subthemes 'Being processed', 'Insensitivity to cultural practices', 'The space to care' directly supports 'language, culture, expectations, system challenges'.

verified.resolved_title: Illuminating health aspects for immigrant Thai women in Swedish transnational marriages.
verified.note: 'Forty immigrant Thai women who currently or previously had a Swedish spouse were recruited' confirms n=40. Abstract confirms 'emotional abuse', 'physical violence', 'transnational family duties', dependence on faith/Buddhist concept of karma (spiritual coping), and cultural-role conflict (failing hopes/duties as a wife in target culture) -- all elements of the claim are directly supported.

verified.resolved_title: Exploring symptoms perception and barriers to medication adherence among Thai Muslim patients with non-communicable diseases in a rural community in southern Thailand: a mixed-methods study.
verified.note: Mixed-methods (138 quantitative + 22 qualitative + 10 HCW focus group), rural southern Thailand. Confirms Ramadan-related medication-adherence barrier and symptom-perception link to non-adherence tied to social/cultural context, exactly as claimed.

verified.resolved_title: The edutainment program on knowledge, perception, and uptake of cervical cancer screening among Muslim women in Southern Thailand: a quasi experimental study.
verified.note: Quasi-experimental (intervention n=42, control n=41). Confirms significant increases in knowledge/perception and uptake nearly doubled (90.47% vs 51.21%) -- matches claim of 'increased knowledge, perception and uptake of cervical cancer screening'.

verified.resolved_title: Religious affiliation and disparities in risk of non-communicable diseases and health behaviours: findings from the fourth Thai National Health Examination Survey.
verified.note: NHES IV (2009), n=20,450 (807 Muslim, 3.9%). Adjusted-OR comparisons confirm 'religious affiliation ... and NCD risk / health behaviours after adjustment' as claimed (deep-fried food OR=1.35, packaged snacks OR=1.55, hypercholesterolemia control OR=2.95, all adjusted).

verified.resolved_title: Muslim mothers' experiences in taking care of children with open heart surgery: A qualitative study in Southern Thailand.
verified.relevance_caution: This is a qualitative study of Muslim mothers coping with a child's congenital-heart-disease surgery and postoperative care via faith/patience/family/professional support -- a caregiving-of-a-sick-child context, not premarital counselling or reproductive/marital health. Cite only as general context on faith-based coping among Thai Muslim families in a clinical setting, not as direct evidence for a premarital programme.
verified.note: Abstract confirms 12 Muslim mothers, in-depth interviews, themes of 'Strengthening faith and trust in God', 'Cultivating patience and resilience', and 'social support systems' (healthcare professionals + family) -- matches claim's 'faith, patience, family and professional support as coping' exactly. Setting is Yala area is plausible (southern Thailand) though province name 'Yala' is not stated verbatim in the abstract itself -- verify against full text if the province name is load-bearing.

verified.resolved_title: Does cultural competence training for health professionals impact culturally and linguistically diverse patient outcomes? A systematic review of the literature.
verified.note: Exact match: 'Of 7879 unique studies identified, five met inclusion criteria' and 'patient health outcomes did not improve significantly in any study' -- verbatim support for '7,879 records -> 5 studies' and 'no clear patient-health outcome improvement'.

verified.resolved_title: Systematic review of Indigenous cultural safety training interventions for healthcare professionals in Australia, Canada, New Zealand and the United States.
verified.note: Covers Australia, Canada, New Zealand, United States as claimed. 'Study outcomes were primarily learner oriented and focused on self-reported changes in knowledge, awareness, beliefs, attitudes and/or the confidence and skills' and 'involvement of local Indigenous communities ... was limited' and conclusion calls for research 'focused on observed clinical outcomes' -- directly supports 'outcomes mostly provider knowledge/awareness/confidence; weak community involvement and clinical outcomes'.

verified.resolved_title: Culturally safe healthcare: changing the lens from provider control to patient agency.
verified.note: Second author confirmed as Zhuang Jie -- 'Bresnahan & Zhuang' attribution is correct. Title and abstract state verbatim: 'an important paradigm shift from provider control to patients who feel safe voicing health concerns' and conclusion 'CSH offers a paradigm shift from provider control to marginalized patients' experience' -- directly supports the 'provider control to patient agency' framing claim. It is a scoping review (21 articles, 2019-2023, modified PRISMA), matching 'scoping review' label.

verified.resolved_title: Physician-Patient Language Discordance and Poor Health Outcomes: A Systematic Scoping Review.
verified.note: 'A total of 15 articles (84,750 participants) were included' matches '84,750 participants' exactly. 'Eight studies (53%) showed a significant negative association between language discordance and at least one clinical outcome' and conclusion 'Over half the evidence collated showed that physician-patient language concordance was associated with better health clinical outcomes' -- supports 'more than half of studies found worse outcomes' (with discordance framing).

verified.resolved_title: Interpreter services and effect on healthcare - a systematic review of the impact of different types of interpreters on patient outcome.
verified.note: 'in-person professional interpreter resulting in highest satisfaction and communication, reaffirming that any interpreter is better than none' -- directly supports 'professional interpreters better satisfaction/communication; no interpreter worse'. 29 reports reviewed.

verified.resolved_title: A systematic review of whether the number of linguistic errors in medical interpretation is associated with the use of professional vs ad hoc interpreters.
verified.note: Explicit recommendation #1: 'Professional in-person interpretation should be the first choice in language-discordant medical consultations' plus 'the number of interpreting errors was significantly lower when using [professional] than family members for [ad hoc interpretation]' -- directly supports 'professional first choice; family/friends risk errors'.

verified.resolved_title: Access of migrant women to sexual and reproductive health services: A systematic review.
verified.note: Exact match: '28 articles were included' and 'lack of information (57%), followed by language issues (43%), cultural differences (39%), economic status (25%), administrative barriers (25%) and discrimination (14%)' -- verbatim support for '28 studies; barriers: information 57%, language 43%, cultural differences 39%'.

verified.resolved_title: Factors influencing sexual and reproductive health of Muslim women: a systematic review.
verified.note: Exact match: 'Fifty-nine studies were included from 22 countries' matches '59 studies, 22 countries' exactly. Abstract confirms contraception-knowledge gaps, religious/cultural interpretation as barriers, and structural barriers (family/husband opposition, stigma) as claimed.

verified.resolved_title: The Impact of Culture on Access to and Utilisation of Maternity Care Amongst Muslim Women in High-Income Countries: A Qualitative Systematic Review.
verified.journal: BJOG: An International Journal of Obstetrics and Gynaecology
verified.note: Meta-ethnography confirmed ('Meta-ethnography was used to develop new concepts'), 2025, high-income countries setting explicitly stated. Four themes 'Religious influences', 'Sociocultural interactions', 'Healthcare as a culture', 'Disrupted communication' match claim verbatim, plus 'cultural insensitivity ... and cultural stereotyping' supports 'insensitivity and stereotyping'.

verified.resolved_title: Public health, policy, and clinical interventions to improve perinatal care for migrant women and infants in high-income countries: a systematic review.
verified.note: Journal, year and content (public health/policy/clinical interventions for perinatal care of migrant women in high-income countries) all match claim exactly.

verified.resolved_title: Association between language discordance and unplanned hospital readmissions or emergency department revisits: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
verified.note: Journal and content match claim exactly: systematic review and meta-analysis of language discordance vs. 28/30-day hospital readmission and ED revisit (7-day/72-hour pediatric).

overall_note: All 19 PMIDs resolve to real, correctly-cited PubMed records; every attached claim (including the strict numeric checks -- 7,879 records -> 5 studies for PMID 35964378; 84,750 participants / >half for PMID 33816420; 28 studies with 57%/43%/39% for PMID 39243595; 59 studies/22 countries for PMID 32138744; 101 studies for PMID 36006258; n=40 for PMID 38867221; and the Bresnahan & Zhuang 'provider control to patient agency' framing for PMID 38426444, second author Zhuang Jie confirmed) is directly and precisely supported by the retrieved abstract text -- no fabricated or misattributed citations found in this batch. One item needs a wording FIX: PMID 36006258's claim that reproductive/maternal health is 'among the most-studied categories' should be qualified, since the abstract shows it is the second-most-studied domain (n=31) behind general health (n=42), not an unqualified top category. One relevance caution: PMID 40256382 (Muslim mothers of children after open-heart surgery) is a real, well-supported study but its topic (pediatric cardiac surgery caregiving) is a stretch for a premarital-programme literature review; the synthesiser should cite it only as general context on faith-based coping in Thai Muslim clinical settings, not as direct evidence for premarital-programme content. This verification used only the abstract text retrieved via NCBI E-utilities efetch; full-text claims beyond the abstract (e.g., the exact province name 'Yala' for PMID 40256382) were not independently checked and should be confirmed against full text if load-bearing.
